findings.where: First screen, Mark's photograph at the lectern (desktop and phone), and the same photograph in the Motion section
findings.fault: The photograph sits on a wide, soft drop shadow even when it is at rest. A shadow like that tells a visitor that something floats above the page or can be clicked, but this picture is a still exhibit. Nothing else on the page has a shadow, so the effect looks like a generic web card. It does not look like a framed object in a well-set brief.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who asked for a page that reads like a legal journal and for nothing slick. A visitor may also try clicking the raised picture and find that nothing happens.

findings.where: Article specimen, the caption under the radio-interview photograph, compared with the caption under the hero photograph
findings.fault: The two captions are treated differently. Under the hero photograph, the italic serif title sits on its own line, with the small sans placeholder note tightly spaced under it. In the article, the italic title and the sans note run together on one line at body-text spacing. The small sans line then wraps with a full body line of space under it, so it looks loose and detached. The article caption is the one Angélique will copy.
findings.who_objects: The founder and Angélique. The brief asks the article specimen to show that a caption keeps to the page's rhythm when she adds one, and here the same part is set two ways.

findings.where: Article specimen, the 'Download' button on the lecture row, compared with 'Write to me' on the first screen
findings.fault: There are two button shapes on one page. The main action, 'Write to me', is a square-cornered filled block. The minor 'Download' action is a fully rounded outline pill with an icon. The only rounded shape on the page goes to the least important control, and it brings an app-style look into a page that is otherwise square-edged like a printed document.
findings.who_objects: The founder. Two button styles look like two design kits mixed together, and the pill pulls the journal look toward a tech product.

findings.where: The email address: next to 'Write to me' on the first screen (desktop and phone), and in the footer
findings.fault: The same address, as the same mailto link, is set two ways. On the first screen it is an ink serif with a grey hairline underline. In the footer it is a blue sans with a blue underline. 'Replay the entrance' is a third version: a blue semibold sans. The tile's palette says the house blue is the link colour, but the most important link on the page does not use it.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who is judging whether this look holds together as a system. A visitor also loses the one consistent cue for what can be clicked.

findings.where: Article specimen, the title 'The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law' (desktop)
findings.fault: The display title breaks at the hyphen inside 'Public-Private', so 'Public-' ends the first line and the name of the subject is split in two. On a phone the compound stays whole.
findings.who_objects: Mark and the founder. In a heading set like a legal journal, splitting the key term looks careless, and the term is the subject of the article.
